query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy is a solid refrigeration working medium that exhibits a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor load-bearing integrity and tends to crack. What single intervention could increase its integrity while preserving caloric performance in these operating regimes? State one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its proposed mechanism, predicted integrity and caloric outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, applicable field, pressure, temperature, and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with explicit results that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a minor amount of carbon during alloy processing to promote in‐situ formation of fine SiC nanoprecipitates will enhance the load-bearing integrity of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 while preserving its large caloric response under applied magnetic and pressure fields.
generation.material_initial_state: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 produced in its as‐cast, single‐phase state that shows a strong caloric effect but poor crack resistance and load-bearing performance.
generation.intervention: Add approximately 1–2 wt% carbon during the melting/processing step so that the available silicon reacts to form a fine dispersion of SiC precipitates.
generation.conditions: Tested under refrigeration operating conditions near room temperature with controlled applied magnetic and pressure fields, and under mechanical loads near typical service levels for refrigeration devices.
generation.structural_mediator: In-situ formed, finely dispersed SiC nanoparticles within the alloy matrix.
generation.mechanism: The SiC nanoprecipitates are expected to act as crack arrestors and dispersion-strengthening agents. They inhibit crack propagation and enhance fracture toughness by impeding dislocation motion without substantially interfering with the order–disorder transitions responsible for the caloric effects.
generation.predicted_outcome: The modified alloy will exhibit a significant increase in mechanical integrity (improved fracture toughness and tensile strength) while maintaining a caloric performance (entropy change under magnetic/pressure fields) similar to that of the unmodified alloy.
generation.baseline: The unmodified (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy, which has a high caloric effect but suffers from poor load-bearing properties and crack susceptibility.
generation.boundary: The predicted improvements are expected when operating near room temperature under the applied magnetic and pressure fields relevant to solid-state refrigeration, and under mechanical loading conditions that do not exceed the processing window for the dispersion strengthening effect.
generation.uncertainty: The exact volume fraction and distribution of SiC precipitates required to optimize strength improvement without affecting the caloric phase transition are not precisely known, and there is uncertainty as to whether even a low level of precipitates might slightly perturb the caloric response.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two batches of (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy: one following the standard procedure and one with an additional 1–2 wt% carbon to promote in-situ SiC precipitate formation. Characterize both batches using microstructural analysis (e.g., TEM/SEM to detect and quantify precipitates). Conduct mechanical testing (measuring fracture toughness and tensile strength) and performance evaluations of the caloric effect (assessing entropy change under applied magnetic and pressure fields at room temperature).
measurements: Microstructural analysis (size, distribution, and volume fraction of SiC precipitates)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the carbon-modified alloy does not show a statistically significant enhancement in mechanical integrity (e.g., less than a ~15% increase in fracture toughness or tensile strength) or if its caloric performance (ΔS under applied fields) deviates by more than ±10% from the unmodified alloy, the hypothesis will be considered falsified.

cited_evidence.text: FeCrNiCu based high entropy alloy matrix composites were fabricated with addition of Si and C by vacuum electromagnetic induction melting. The primary goal of this research was to analyze the reaction mechanism, microstructure, mechanical properties at room temperature and strengthening mechanism of the composites with addition of Si and C. The reaction mechanism of powders containing (Si, Ni and C) was analyzed, only one reaction occurred (i.e., Si + C → SiC) and its activation energy is 1302.8 kJ/mol. The new composites consist of a face centered cubic (FCC) structured matrix reinforced by submicron sized SiC particles. The addition of Si and C enhances the hardness from 351.4 HV to 626.4 HV and the tensile strength from 565.5 MPa to 846.0 MPa, accompanied by a slight decrease in the plasticity. The main strengthening mechanisms of SiC/FeCrNiCu composites were discussed based on dislocation strengthening, load bearing effect, Orowan mechanism and solid solution hardening, whose contributions to the tensile strength increase are 58.6%, 6.3%, 14.3% and 20.8%, respectively.
